standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the hero! Thank you so much for saving us from Gadderanks. And the town is looking lovely as well. You've done a great job!

steps.npc: I'm Aurel the village store owner.

steps.player: Can you open the shop for me please?

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

standard-dialogue.npc: Oh, not much really. We're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place.
Hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey across the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

standard-dialogue.npc: Not as far as I know. We have some basic amenities now which is so very useful and we're all incredibly grateful to you.
I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

if-the-player-has-lost-the-gadderhammer.npc: Hey it's the hero! Thank you so much for saving us from Gadderanks. And the town is looking lovely as well. You've done a great job!

steps.npc: Hmm, how careless of you! However, you're in luck! Someone found it earlier and sold it to me.
Now I can pass the hammer back to you for the remarkably cheap price of 3000 gold coins. Deal?

steps.text: If the player is not carrying enough coins:

steps.player: But I don't have 3000 coins on me?

steps.npc: So that means you can't have it then! Come back when you have 3000 coins.

steps.text: If the player is carrying enough coins:

options.text: Okay, I'll pay 3000 coins for the hammer.

steps.player: Oayk, I'll pay 3000 coins for the hammer.

steps.npc: A good deal and I'm sure of it!

options.text: No thanks, I'll leave it. 3000 coins is too much to pay.

steps.player: No thanks, I'll leave it, 3000 coins is too much to pay.

steps.npc: Very good then! I'll have no guilty conscience in offering it to other adventurers that frequent my shop then. Many thanks for your time and good day to ya sir.

options.text: Why does the hammer cost so much?

steps.player: Why does the hammer cost so much?

steps.npc: So much! That's cheap! The adventurer I bought it from wanted twice as much but I managed to knock him down to a reasonable price.

options.text: Okay, I'll pay 3000 coins for the hammer.
No thanks, I'll leave it. 3000 coins is too much to pay.
Is there anything I can do to help out?

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.npc: I'm Aurel, the village store owner.

steps.player: Can you open the shop for me please?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.
